from: A country's sector shares of employment over twenty years are: primary 34% to 19%, secondary 21% to 18%, tertiary and quaternary together 45% to 63%. State what has happened to the relative importance of each sector, explain two reasons for the change, and explain one consequence for the people who worked in the declining sector.
to: A country's sector shares of employment over twenty years are: primary 34% to 19%, secondary 21% to 18%, tertiary and quaternary together 45% to 63%. Identify what has happened to the relative importance of each sector, explain two reasons for the change, and explain one consequence for the people who worked in the declining sector.
why: State is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify for the first part. It combines several parts, so no single tariff is claimed.

from: Frans has traded as a sole trader for nine years installing solar systems. He now employs six people, holds N$900 000 of stock on credit from a single supplier, and has been offered a contract to fit systems at forty schools, worth N$11 million over two years, with payment ninety days after each installation is certified. He owns a house worth about N$2.3 million. His bank has said it would advance working capital against the contract but would want personal security. Analyse the liability position Frans is in, and recommend what he should do before signing the contract.
to: Frans has traded as a sole trader for nine years installing solar systems. He now employs six people, holds N$900 000 of stock on credit from a single supplier, and has been offered a contract to fit systems at forty schools, worth N$11 million over two years, with payment ninety days after each installation is certified. He owns a house worth about N$2.3 million. His bank has said it would advance working capital against the contract but would want personal security. Analyse the liability position Frans is in, and evaluate what he should do before signing the contract.
why: Recommend is not used on the current AS papers; the judgement is now asked for with Evaluate. The card keeps its Analyse part, so it pairs the two parts of a Paper 1 Section B question (8 + 12) and no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Forty women in the Kunene region harvest and press marula oil. At present each sells to traders who call at the village. A development agency has offered to fund a press and a store, and asks them to choose between forming a producer co-operative owned by the forty, and forming a social enterprise run by a small board that would buy their fruit at a guaranteed price and reinvest its surplus in the community. Analyse the difference between the two options for these women, and recommend which they should choose.
